classification.difficultyReason: Several linked decisions using the demonstrated definitions or procedures. The quadratic denominator factors into exactly the two other denominators; retain both excluded values and check the solution is permitted.

answer.short:
$x=\dfrac{11}{5}$; original domain $x\ne-1,2$.

Factorise $x^2-x-2=(x+1)(x-2)$ and clear the common denominator.
answer.worked:
Since $x^2-x-2=(x+1)(x-2)$, the original domain is $x\ne-1,2$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2(x-2)+3(x+1)}{(x+1)(x-2)}&=\frac{10}{(x+1)(x-2)}\\2(x-2)+3(x+1)&=10\\2x-4+3x+3&=10\\5x-1&=10\\5x&=11\\x&=\frac{11}{5}.\end{align*}$$
This value is in the original domain.
